items.stem: How does IAS 2 require inventories to be measured?

options.text: At the lower of cost and net realisable value
options.rationale: Correct: inventories are measured at the lower of cost and NRV.

options.text: At the higher of cost and net realisable value
options.rationale: It is the lower, not the higher, of the two.
Selling price is not the measurement basis.

options.text: At replacement cost in all cases
options.rationale: Replacement cost is not the general measurement rule.

items.explanation: Correct: inventories are measured at the lower of cost and NRV.

items.stem: Which TWO cost formulas are permitted by IAS 2 for interchangeable inventory items? (Select TWO.)

options.rationale: Correct: weighted average cost is permitted.
LIFO is not permitted under IAS 2.
NIFO is not a permitted cost formula.

items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: A retailer writes a product line down to net realisable value, then the selling price recovers above original cost. By how much may the write-down be reversed?

options.text: Only up to the original cost; inventory is never carried above cost
options.rationale: Correct: a reversal is limited so the carrying amount does not exceed original cost.

options.text: Up to the new, higher selling price
options.rationale: Inventory cannot be carried above cost even if selling price exceeds it.

options.text: The write-down can never be reversed
options.rationale: Reversals are permitted when NRV recovers.

options.text: Up to double the original cost
options.rationale: There is no basis for carrying above cost.

items.explanation: Correct: a reversal is limited so the carrying amount does not exceed original cost.
